newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya police fire teargas at Nairobi protesters.
newsitem.headline: Kenya police fire teargas at Nairobi protesters.

text.p: Kenya security forces fought pitched battles with protesters on Saturday and deployed thousands of heavily armed troops after breaking up an opposition and church rally.
A series of battles brought central Nairobi to a standstill as police and paramilitary units firing teargas grenades and wielding clubs charged protesters opposed to President Daniel arap Moi.
Protesters smashed shop windows, stoned cars and burned a national flag after security forces fired teargas at around 2,000 people in central Uhuru Park as they started the rally with prayers.
Police armed with automatic rifles, many in full riot gear, deployed across the city centre. Troops ringed parliament and the state-owned radio and television stations.

"We are here to defy the illegal law called the Public Order Act because it is against the constitution, which states that there is freedom of assembly and association," opposition FORD-Asili MP Martin Shikuku told Reuters at the rally.

The National Convention Assembly (NCA), an umbrella for church leaders and opposition parties, called the rally to press for a minimum package of constitutional reform before elections later this year.
Diplomats, human rights groups and opposition politicians accuse the Kenya government of deploying the Public Order Act on behalf of the ruling Kenya African National Union (Kanu) party.
President Moi must call presidential and parliamentary elections by the end of the year, pitting KANU against an opposition divided along ethnic, political and personal lines.
On Friday the government declared the rally illegal and warned the public not to attend.
Opposition activists including FORD-Asili's Ngengi Muigai were arrested near the Westlands district as they approached the city centre, an eyewitness said. There were no further details of arrests.
An aide to leading opposition politician, Kenneth Matiba, said his boss was meeting other opposition figures at a hideout in the city to plan their next move.
The government had warned the public not to attend the rally and said anyone attending would face the full force of the law.

Matiba, a leading opposition leader and proponent of constitutional change, told Reuters through his spokesman: "We will make the city hell for Moi and his cronies. I will not sleep tonight because I have to be with the people and this means Moi cannot sleep either because his security will have to keep on briefing him."
Matiba is chairman of FORD-Asili and one of Kenya's leading businessmen.
A convoy carrying Tanzania President Benjamin Mkapa, on a state visit to Kenya, drove through a crowd of demonstrators, who were later clubbed by security forces, a Reuters correspondent said.
A senior police officer said police and paramilitary units were under strict orders to stamp out pockets of lawlessness in the city. "We are acting on high-level orders," the officer said.
A senior Kenya Red Cross official said at 12 p.m. local time (0900 GMT) there were no serious casualties.
Most of the people trying to attend the opposition rally had been turned away outside the city, David Kabeberi, a senior adviser to FORD-Asili leader Kenneth Matiba said.
